newsitem.title: PANAMA: Ecuador's Bucaram keeps low profile during vote.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Bucaram keeps low profile during vote.

text.p: Ecuador's deposed President Abdala Bucaram was keeping a low profile during Sunday's referendum vote seeking to ratify or reject his dismissal, a spokesman said.
"He will be watching the results, but he is going to keep a low profile," spokesman Hatuey Castro said.

Nearly seven million voters in Ecuador will determine whether Bucaram's ouster from office in February on grounds of "mental incompetence" was justified and whether the interim government of President Fabian Alarcon should remain in office until 1998.
Private opinion polls show most voters support Bucaram's removal and favour Alarcon's administration.

Bucaram received political asylum in Panama City along with his family and brother Santiago, who was expelled from Congress with 12 other deputies who were accused of siphoning funds from the national budget.
Ecuador's Supreme Court has issued a warrant for Bucaram's arrest on grounds of misuse of presidential funds.
